posts.body:
Well... this is new.

After plenty of planning, writing, rewriting, changing my mind, and probably making my friend regret agreeing to help me with this in the first place, writtenbyskyk.com is officially live!

This website has been something I've wanted to put together for quite a while, a place where all of my stories can live under one roof, whether they're finished, currently being written, or still waiting impatiently in the back of my head.

There's still plenty I want to add as those stories grow, but for now, I'm incredibly happy to finally have a little corner of the internet to call my own.

And since you're reading this, I suppose the Updates section works too.

Welcome to my worlds!
posts.title: Apparently I have a website now.
Back to Sekari
posts.body:
Hello again! Hope you're all doing well!

It's been a little while since I launched this website, and apparently it hasn't broken yet, so I'm calling that a success.

Now that everything is up and running, I figured it's probably time I actually use this little Updates section for what it was made for: talking about what I'm writing.

And right now, that means going back to Sekari.

"The Last Druid" may be finished, but I'm definitely not finished with its world. Most of my writing time lately has been going into the second book, "The Last Druid: Rising Tide." It picks up immediately after the first book ends, so there wasn't exactly much time for anyone to recover.
I'm sure they'll be fine.
Probably.

Writing a sequel has been a surprisingly different experience from writing the first book. With "The Last Druid," I was still figuring out the world, the characters and, occasionally, what on earth I was actually doing. Now I get to return to all of it already knowing these people, which is both wonderful and mildly inconvenient when they refuse to cooperate with whatever I originally planned for them.

"Rising Tide" lets me explore parts of Sekari that the first book only touched on, bring back people from Zane's past, and spend more time with the five characters at the heart of the story now that they've somehow gone from complete strangers to something resembling a family.
A dysfunctional one, obviously.

There are also some new faces, new places and quite a few things I have been waiting a very long time to write. 
Some of those things are lovely. Some of them are not.
I'm not going to say which.

There's still plenty of "Rising Tide" left to write, and I'm deliberately not putting a deadline on it. For now, I'm enjoying being back with these characters and watching the pile of notes, half-written scenes and questionable decisions slowly turn into an actual book.

~ Sky

posts.title: Still alive. Still writing.
posts.body:
Hello again!

It's been a little while since the last update.

I'd love to tell you that's because I've been locked away somewhere writing thousands upon thousands of words, completely oblivious to the outside world.

Unfortunately, reality has been considerably less dramatic.

A few things in my life have changed recently, and I'm still figuring out what my new routine looks like. Finding the right balance between writing and, you know, everything else has been a bit of a work in progress.

But I'm still writing.

Rising Tide is very much alive and slowly but surely getting longer. I've been making my way through some scenes I've been looking forward to for quite a while, spending more time with characters I probably missed a little too much, and—as usual—discovering that some of my plans were apparently suggestions rather than actual plans.

The characters have opinions.

Unfortunately.

But I'm having the time of my life following them. I don't want to reveal too much, and I don't want to put down a percentage of how far along I am or anything, but after a rather slow start to the book, things are now heating up (literally) as everything goes even further downhill than I originally planned.

But it'll be okay.

Well, depending on how you define "okay."

I'm still figuring out when and where writing fits best into this new rhythm, and it'll probably take some time before everything feels completely normal again.

But honestly?

That's okay.

The book isn't going anywhere. Neither am I.

I'm just finding my footing.

~ Sky

posts.title: Still talking to myself
posts.body:
Hi! Hi! Hi!

Look at me, actually remembering that this Updates section exists.

Growth.

It's only been a little over a week since the last one, but quite a bit has been happening behind the scenes. And, fittingly enough, most of it has involved the new(ish) Behind the Pages section.

When I first added that little corner to the website, I wasn't entirely sure what it would become. I knew I wanted somewhere to talk about the things that don't really belong on a project page. You know, the ideas, decisions, questionable writing habits and everything else that happens somewhere between “I have an idea” and “somehow this is a book now.”

The first article, “How The Last Druid Began,” was exactly that.

Obviously, one wasn't enough.

I've recently finished another one, this time about the slightly chaotic way I plan my stories—or, perhaps more accurately, the way I mostly don't.

There are people who have beautiful timelines, detailed character sheets and entire novels planned before they write Chapter One.

I am not one of those people.

Somehow, it works.

I don't know either.

I'm having a lot of fun figuring out what Behind the Pages can become, though. I don't want it to turn into a traditional writing blog or a collection of advice on how anyone should write. God knows I'm not qualified to tell anyone that.

I'd much rather use it as a place to show you how I do it.

The organized parts.

The chaotic parts.

And, apparently, the notes that make absolutely no sense to anyone except me.

Of course, all of this comes with the quiet hope that someone out there is actually reading these things.

And if you are...

Hi.

I'm glad you're here. Thank you for that.

~ Sky
